newsitem.title: UK: UPS to convert five B727-100s into QC jets.
newsitem.headline: UPS to convert five B727-100s into QC jets.

text.p: In a landmark diversification into passenger operations, United Parcel Service (UPS) plans to convert five of its Boeing 727-100s into quick-change cargo-to-people carriers.
The US parcel express firm wants to win weekend passenger charter traffic from U.S. cruise lines and tour operators to destinations in the U.S., Mexico, Caribbean and Europe.
In an interview at Farnborough, Fredrik Groth, group vice-president for Pemco World Air Services, said conversions would be undertaken by his Denver-based group.
The conversion will focus on the Boeing 727-100s which have been re-engined with Rolls-Royce Tay engines to meet Stage Three noise requirements.
A letter of intent has been signed and final contracts are imminent.
Depending on the success of the QC experiment, UPS's entire fleet of re-engined B727-100s could be similarly adapted. UPS also operates eight 727-200s.
According to Groth, UPS wants to double their utilisation from just over two hours per day to nearer five hours.

Switching original passenger jets converted for parcel carriage back to QC mode, said Groth, involves re-installing air, water, galleys, windows, bins, wall linings and "everything that's passenger-related".

UPS spokesman Ken Shapero said the parcel express firm currently only uses its 727s four nights a week but it wants to be able to switch them for passenger use from Friday AM to Monday PM to generate additional revenues.
Unlike conventional QC arrangements, where galleys and overhead bins stay in place and only seats are removed, UPS wants all passenger facilities stripped out.
The QC switch will take about four hours, said Groth.
The Pemco executive declined to put a price on the initial deal but said it ran into many million of dollars.

Shapero added: "By mid-1997, our proof of concept should have told us whether we can integrate passenger charter business into our core business." - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
